ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm which road the 08:42–08:54 segment was actually driven (Balestier Road corridor or not). If it was not the agreed road, issue a $6.68 Ryde voucher (4.74 km × $1.4098/km [F3][F4][F7], RD-2) within the 30-day window; if it was, the segment is exempt and no refund is due. No account flag (0 upheld disputes in 90 d [F18], RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip — total $40.45, distance $26.80 for 19.01 km, time $8.17, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47 [F7] — so any route-deviation relief runs through RD-2's RydeTAXI branch: only the metered distance units of a non-exempt off-route segment (extra_km × this trip's rate) are refundable, not the whole fare gap. Both advocates agree on this framing [C1][D1].

Two elements are code-settled and bind me. One off-route segment exists, 08:42–08:54, 7.24 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.50 km, adding 4.74 km and reaching up to 1568 m off that route [F3][RD-1]. And RD-4(a) fails: no LTA traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F15][RD-4], so the Central Expressway band-2 record [F12], band-only and ending at 08:42, cannot exempt the segment on its own under RD-4(b) — the driver concedes this [D5][RD-4]. The free-flowing alternative roads at band 5 [F13][F14] reinforce that no traffic excuse is made out.

The single live question is RD-5. The rider's 08:40 message "可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。" [F9] is a genuine rider message answering the driver's 08:39 proposal to go round via Balestier Road [F8], sent before the segment started at 08:42 [F3] on a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10] — consent exists and is timely. But its words are a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation, not a general route choice: under RD-5 it covers driving on Balestier Road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road. Nothing does. The only facts about the path are distance and position data [F3]; the only mention of the road is the driver's post-trip statement [F11], which is a claim and not rider consent [G11]; and no fact places the segment on another named road. That is the named_road_untied situation: G13 fixes the finding as undetermined, which the policy does not convert into an exemption. RD-3 gives no help: the rider named a road, not a place she was stopping at, and no stop was measured in the segment [F9][F3][RD-3].

Because the rider's words are a specific named road rather than "go whichever way is faster", I cannot read the consent as reaching whatever route the driver chose; and because no record ties the segment to Balestier Road, I equally cannot exempt it. The record therefore does not settle whether the 4.74 km extra [F3] was consented to, and that element is outcome-determining: exempt means no_action (zero refund); counts means a $6.68 refund under RD-2. I therefore escalate rather than pick one, and a person decides.

For the human reviewer, the arithmetic if the segment is held non-exempt is: $26.80 ÷ 19.01 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4]; 4.74 km × $1.4098/km = $6.6824 → $6.68 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The billed excess of $7.22 covers 5.12 km [F4][F1], but RD-2 refunds only mileage attributed to a segment, so the 0.38 km remainder is not refundable [C10][D7]. The $0.11 waiting item [F5] is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min [F5][F7]) and RD-3(c) keeps metered waiting with the meter, so it is not waived. No flag_account: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18], so RD-6's precondition is absent [RD-6]. FARE-1 strikes nothing — no surge (1.0×) [F6] and only published items in the itemisation [F7][FARE-1].

Safety screen: I read every chat message [F8][F9], the driver's statement [F11] and the rider's complaint; the strongest rider wording is her uncertainty about which road was taken, and there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — safety_concern none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The elements the trace marks settled (segment, distance, fare rate, timestamps) are all on the record [F1][F3][F4][F7][F10]; the gap is the road-name linkage for the agreed route [F9][F3], which is the RD-5/G13 element I cannot read.
